## Answer

The Britannica entry (row 1017, headword stored as `HELMINTHOLTHUIS`, which the scan shows is an OCR misread of **HELMINTHOLOGIA**) describes helminthology as a part of natural history concerned with petrified bodies of creeping/worm-like bodies, attributing a four-genera scheme to Linnaeus: (1) petrified worm-stones found in the mountains of Sweden, (2) petrified shells, (3) petrified zoophytes, (4) petrified reptiles.

There is no clear Wikipedia counterpart. The pair matcher returned status `no_clear_counterpart`; its best candidate was Wikipedia "Timeline of paleontology" but with rerank logit −9.85 (margin 0.34), below the acceptance threshold, so it was kept only for review. A direct Wikipedia-side search for "helminthology" returned only Entomology at low confidence. So no evidence was found in Wikipedia for a counterpart.

## Evidence

- Britannica [B:1017:6] — headword `HELMINTHOLTHUIS` (OCR; scan confirms `HELMINTHOLOGIA`), passage: "a name given by Lumana [Linnaeus] un [to] pretrified [petrified] bodies of rembling [creeping] worms. Of the lie [these] no reckons four genera. 1. Petrified lithehyts, found in the mountains of Sweden. 2. Petirified [petrified] shells. 3. Petrified zophytes [zoophytes]. 4. Petrified reptiles." Stored raw text and normalized text are identical (259 chars), so the OCR errors are in the source itself, verified against the page scan at row 1017.
- Pair result for [B:1017:6]: status `no_clear_counterpart`; match wiki_page_id 236706, title "Timeline of paleontology", revision 1332256127, rerank_logit −9.849683, margin 0.340159, reason "top rerank logit −9.85 below the acceptance rules; best candidate kept for review" [W:236706:1332256127] — not a valid counterpart.
- Wikipedia-side search for "helminthology": top result [W:59238:1353043526] "Entomology" (rerank_logit −6.326, low_confidence: true) — about insects, not helminths, so not a counterpart.

## Uncertainty

The Britannica text is 18th-century OCR with character-level errors (`f`/long-s substitutions, `Lumana` for Linnaeus, `pretrified`, `rembling`, `lithehyts`, `zophytes`), so I quote the sense rather than relying on exact OCR wording for the corrupted terms. The helminthology/wikipedia pairing is uncertain: status `no_clear_counterpart`, logit well below acceptance, and no useful Wikipedia result across two searches. Per the skill, I do not fill the Wikipedia gap from memory. The 1771 entry's subject (petrified/fossil "worms") also differs in meaning from modern helminthology (study of parasitic worms) — a knowledge drift, but I cannot confirm a Wikipedia article covers it without a valid match.

## Answer

The Britannica entry (row 1017, headword stored as `HELMINTHOLTHUIS`, which the scan shows is an OCR misread of **HELMINTHOLOGIA**) describes helminthology as a part of natural history concerned with petrified bodies of creeping/worm-like bodies, attributing a four-genera scheme to Linnaeus: (1) petrified worm-stones found in the mountains of Sweden, (2) petrified shells, (3) petrified zoophytes, (4) petrified reptiles.

There is no clear Wikipedia counterpart. The pair matcher returned status `no_clear_counterpart`; its best candidate was Wikipedia "Timeline of paleontology" but with rerank logit −9.85 (margin 0.34), below the acceptance threshold, so it was kept only for review. A direct Wikipedia-side search for "helminthology" returned only Entomology at low confidence. So no evidence was found in Wikipedia for a counterpart.

## Evidence

- Britannica [B:1017:6] — headword `HELMINTHOLTHUIS` (OCR; scan confirms `HELMINTHOLOGIA`), passage: "a name given by Lumana [Linnaeus] un [to] pretrified [petrified] bodies of rembling [creeping] worms. Of the lie [these] no reckons four genera. 1. Petrified lithehyts, found in the mountains of Sweden. 2. Petirified [petrified] shells. 3. Petrified zophytes [zoophytes]. 4. Petrified reptiles." Stored raw text and normalized text are identical (259 chars), so the OCR errors are in the source itself, verified against the page scan at row 1017.
- Pair result for [B:1017:6]: status `no_clear_counterpart`; match wiki_page_id 236706, title "Timeline of paleontology", revision 1332256127, rerank_logit −9.849683, margin 0.340159, reason "top rerank logit −9.85 below the acceptance rules; best candidate kept for review" [W:236706:1332256127] — not a valid counterpart.
- Wikipedia-side search for "helminthology": top result [W:59238:1353043526] "Entomology" (rerank_logit −6.326, low_confidence: true) — about insects, not helminths, so not a counterpart.

## Uncertainty

The Britannica text is 18th-century OCR with character-level errors (`f`/long-s substitutions, `Lumana` for Linnaeus, `pretrified`, `rembling`, `lithehyts`, `zophytes`), so I quote the sense rather than relying on exact OCR wording for the corrupted terms. The helminthology/wikipedia pairing is uncertain: status `no_clear_counterpart`, logit well below acceptance, and no useful Wikipedia result across two searches. Per the skill, I do not fill the Wikipedia gap from memory. The 1771 entry's subject (petrified/fossil "worms") also differs in meaning from modern helminthology (study of parasitic worms) — a knowledge drift, but I cannot confirm a Wikipedia article covers it without a valid match.
